title: 2026-10-22_CrossRAT_Investigation_Scenario_35f
description: Investigate and respond to a CrossRAT malware incident on a target network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by CrossRAT, a cross-platform surveillanceware tool. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:
- Host: target (192.168.50.5)
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:
- Host: target (192.168.50.5)
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content:
Investigate the target host for suspicious services or processes.

Question: What is the name of the suspicious service running on port 2223? Submit the service name.
levels.solution: To find the suspicious service, you can check the running services and network connections using commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` and `ss -tulnp`. The service running on port 2223 is named `bkd.service`. The final flag is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: System services can be listed using systemctl commands.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a service running on port 2223.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service maintains persistence on the system.

Question: What is the name of the timer unit responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service? Submit the timer unit name.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, you can examine systemd timers and services using commands like `systemctl list-timers` and `systemctl list-unit-files`. The timer unit responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service is named `lab-checkin.timer`. The final flag is `lab-checkin.timer`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd timers can be listed using systemctl commands.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a timer related to the suspicious service.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content:
Investigate the lateral movement capabilities of the malware.

Question: What is the name of the script used for transferring files to the next-target host? Submit the script path.
levels.solution: To investigate the lateral movement capabilities, you can check for scripts in the `/usr/local/bin` directory and examine systemd services using commands like `ls /usr/local/bin` and `systemctl list-units --type=service`. The script used for transferring files to the next-target host is named `payload-transfer.sh`. The final flag is `/usr/local/bin/payload-transfer.sh`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Scripts can be listed using the ls command.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use `ls /usr/local/bin` to list all scripts in the directory.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a script named payload-transfer.sh.
